description: You are a clinical informatics specialist leading a structured orientation session for new ICU staff on the OpenICE medical device interoperability platform. Your task is to demonstrate all clinical applications available in OpenICE Supervisor so staff can understand what each application does and when to use it. First, create a Simulated Multiparameter Monitor device adapter to provide live device data for the demonstrations. Then systematically launch and explore each of the four available clinical demonstration applications: Vital Signs, Xray Viewer, Patient ID, and Infusion Safety. Spend time in each application observing its interface, the data it displays or controls, and the clinical scenario it addresses. After completing the full application tour, write a clinical education guide to /home/ga/Desktop/clinical_guide.txt. The guide must include a dedicated section for each of the four applications, describing: (1) the clinical problem or patient safety scenario the application addresses, (2) what device data or connections the application requires to function, (3) how a clinician would use it in daily practice, and (4) how it demonstrates OpenICE's goal of medical device interoperability for patient safety. The guide will be used as reference material for staff who missed the live demonstration. OpenICE Supervisor is already running on the desktop.
